title: eDKM: An Efficient and Accurate Train-Time Weight Clustering for Large Language Models
problem: Differentiable KMeans (DKM) weight clustering achieves state-of-the-art compression accuracy for LLMs but its memory complexity makes train-time application to billion-parameter LLMs nearly impossible, requiring far more GPU memory than available on any single device.
motivation: Weight clustering (non-linear quantization) is natively supported on modern smartphones and offers high compression ratios for on-device LLM inference, but the training overhead of DKM has blocked its application at LLM scale.
method: Compressing a neural network by clustering weights (grouping similar weights together) requires an algorithm that saves temporary values during backpropagation (the step where weights get updated) to calculate how much each weight should change. eDKM shrinks the memory this requires in two ways: uniquification detects and removes duplicate copies of the same temporary data before offloading it to CPU storage, and sharding splits the remaining large data into smaller pieces that compress better. Together these techniques reduce memory use per decoder layer by 130x, enabling a 7B LLaMA model to be compressed to 3 bits per weight and fine-tuned on a standard GPU.
key_novelty: The core insight is removing duplicate copies of temporary data (uniquification) and breaking large data structures called tensors into smaller partitions (sharding) during CPU offload of the backward pass, reducing memory by 130x per decoder layer and making train-time weight clustering practical for 7B-parameter language models.
contributions: Identification of DKM's backward-pass tensor redundancy and memory explosion as the key barrier to LLM-scale weight clustering.
Uniquification technique: deduplication of identical CPU-offloaded tensors during DKM backward pass.
Sharding technique: partitioning large tensors to further reduce memory footprint.
130x memory reduction per decoder layer; LLaMA 7B compressed from 12.6 GB to 2.5 GB (3b/weight) with competitive accuracy (PIQA 77.7%, Winogrande 66.1%).

metrics.other: 130x reduction in train-time memory per decoder layer; model size: 12.6 GB to 2.5 GB

limitations: The compression ratio and accuracy trade-offs at sub-3b granularity or for larger models (13B, 70B) are not evaluated; mobile device inference latency improvements are not directly measured.
primary_theme: Memory-efficient train-time weight clustering for LLM compression
